hints: Focus on what causes the small M+1 peak in a mass spectrum, it is almost entirely due to the 1.1% natural abundance of carbon-13.
Convert the 13:1 ratio into a percentage, the M+1 peak is about 7.7% of the size of the M peak, then ask how many carbons would give that total.
Use the quick rule that % of M+1 is about 1.1 multiplied by number of carbons, then work out the molecular formula of each named compound to find the match.
walkthrough:
**Understand the M+1 peak**

Think of the M+1 peak as molecules that are 1 mass unit heavier because they contain one heavier isotope.

For organic compounds containing C, H and O, this is almost all due to $^{13}\text{C}$, which has about 1.1% abundance. Each carbon atom adds about 1.1% to the size of M+1 relative to M.

**Find the number of carbons from the ratio**

Here the ratio M : M+1 is 13 : 1, so M+1 is 1/13 of M.

Calculation rule:
$$\frac{\text{abundance of M+1}}{\text{abundance of M}} \times 100 \approx 1.1 \times n$$ where $n$ is number of C atoms.
$$\frac{1}{13} \times 100 \approx 7.7\% \approx 1.1 \times n$$
$$n \approx \frac{7.7}{1.1} \approx 7$$ So compound Z must contain 7 carbon atoms.

**Count carbons in each option**

Now just write the molecular formula for each name.

A butyl butanoate: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}\text{O}_2$, so 8 carbons.

B hexan-3-one: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$, so 6 carbons.

C 2,2,3-trimethylhexane: hexane (6) + 3 methyls = $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{20}$, so 9 carbons.

D 3,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol: pentane (5) + 2 methyls = $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{16}\text{O}$, so 7 carbons.

**Conclude the identity**

Only the 7-carbon compound gives an M+1 peak of about 7.7% of M, which matches the 13:1 ratio.

Therefore Z is 3,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol.

options.A: Butyl butanoate is C8H16O2 with 8 carbons. It would give M+1 of about 8 x 1.1 = 8.8%, a ratio of about 11.4:1, not 13:1. Students choosing this may have miscounted carbons in the ester.
options.B: Hexan-3-one is C6H12O with 6 carbons. It would give M+1 of about 6 x 1.1 = 6.6%, a ratio of about 15:1. This is too small an M+1 peak for the observed ratio.
options.C: 2,2,3-trimethylhexane is C9H20 with 9 carbons. It would give M+1 of about 9 x 1.1 = 9.9%, a ratio of about 10:1. This M+1 peak would be noticeably larger than observed.
options.D: 3,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol is C7H16O with 7 carbons. Expected M+1 is about 7 x 1.1 = 7.7% of M, which is 100/7.7 = 13:1. This matches the data perfectly.
